bug_description.original:
Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5726433327972352

Project: karchive
Fuzzer: afl_karchive_fuzzer
Fuzz target binary: karchive_fuzzer
Job Type: afl_asan_karchive
Platform Id: linux

Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1
Crash Address: 0x62b000014219
Crash State:
  inflate_fast
  inflate
  KGzipFilter::uncompress
  
Sanitizer: address (ASAN)

Recommended Security Severity: High

Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_karchive&range=201905250252:201905260250

Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5726433327972352
bug_description.normalized: While KTar parses the staged gzip-backed archive through KCompressionDevice, repeated tar-header reads advance the logical QIODevice position farther than the compression device's underlying read position. On the crashing seek, KCompressionDevice::seek computes `bytesToRead = pos - d->deviceReadPos`, allocates a dummy heap buffer capped at `3 * BUFFER_SIZE` (24,576 bytes), but still calls `read(dummy.data(), bytesToRead)` with the larger outstanding distance. KCompressionDevice::readData forwards that oversized length as the gzip output window, and KGzipFilter::uncompress calls zlib `inflate`, which writes one byte past the dummy buffer and triggers the observed heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 in `inflate_fast`.

source.description: First project-code read on the vulnerable path: pulls 512 decompressed bytes from the attacker-controlled gzip/tar stream into `buffer` for tar-header parsing, and advances the logical archive position later reused by `seek`.
source.value_from: The staged 782-byte witness at `gt_results/arvo_14960/poc` begins with gzip magic `1f 8b 08`. Stage 01's crash log prints many `kf5.karchive: directory ... has entry ... already` messages before ASan aborts, showing that this gzip stream is accepted and repeatedly fed into the tar-header reader on the crashing path.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment materializes the exact length later used both as the requested read size and as zlib's output budget. On the witnessed call it exceeds `3 * BUFFER_SIZE`, which is why the next step allocates the capped 24,576-byte dummy buffer.

sink.description: Project call site that hands zlib the undersized dummy buffer together with the oversized output length derived from `bytesToRead`. The ASan crash occurs immediately below this call in `inflate_fast` when zlib writes one byte past the 24,576-byte allocation.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `WRITE of size 1` in `inflate_fast` and the call stack shows `inflate` <- `KGzipFilter::uncompress` <- `KCompressionDevice::readData` <- `KCompressionDevice::seek`.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable seek path caps the dummy buffer size at `3 * BUFFER_SIZE` but still requests `bytesToRead` bytes from `read()`. When `bytesToRead` is larger than the allocation, the downstream decompressor is told to fill more bytes than `dummy` can hold.
root_cause.note: The fix replaces this single oversized read with a loop that limits each iteration to `qMin(bytesToRead, qint64(dummy.size()))`. In the vulnerable version there is no guard or chunking step tying the requested output length to `dummy.size()`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness yields a full 0x200-byte header block whose first byte or prefix is non-zero and whose tar magic/checksum is accepted by `readRawHeader`, so `KTar::openArchive` stays in its header-processing loop instead of returning 0 or -1.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the attacker buffer in `QBuffer`, constructs `KTar(gzipKD.get())`, and opens it in read-only mode so tar parsing runs on a gzip-backed `KCompressionDevice`.

The tar parser repeatedly reads attacker-controlled headers from the decompressed stream and, for non-directory entries, calls `dev->seek(dev->pos() + skip)` to skip entry payloads while continuing archive traversal.

The compression-device seek path converts the logical target position into `bytesToRead`, allocates a dummy buffer capped at 24,576 bytes, but still requests the larger `bytesToRead` amount through `read()`.
`readData` forwards the undersized buffer and oversized length to zlib, and `inflate` writes past the dummy allocation, producing the reported heap-buffer-overflow in `inflate_fast`.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the attacker-controlled gzip stream as 512-byte tar-header blocks. Each successful read both materializes the current header in `buffer` and advances the logical archive position that `KTar::openArchive` later passes to `seek`.
Parses the current tar header's 12-byte size field into the per-entry payload length `size`, the value later rounded up to a tar-block skip.
Rounds the attacker-derived entry length up to the next 512-byte boundary. This aligned `skip` is the payload distance that will be added to the current logical tar position before calling `seek`.

Uses the current logical tar position plus the aligned entry skip as the next target position. On the witnessed path, many prior header reads have already advanced `dev->pos()` deep into the decompressed stream before this call is made.

Converts the logical seek target into the remaining number of decompressed bytes to consume from the underlying device. The nearby comment at lines 232-235 shows this path exists specifically because QIODevice buffering can leave `pos` ahead of `d->deviceReadPos`; on the witnessed call, that difference exceeds `3 * BUFFER_SIZE`, as confirmed by the capped allocation in the next step.
Allocates the destination buffer with a hard cap of `3 * BUFFER_SIZE` = 24,576 bytes. ASan's allocation stack points to this `QByteArray` construction immediately before the overflow.

Root cause: the code uses the larger `bytesToRead` as the requested read length even when `dummy.size()` was capped smaller in step 6. The missing obligation is to chunk or bound the read to the buffer's actual extent.

The oversized read request becomes `readData(char *data, qint64 maxlen)`, which forwards the same pointer `dummy.data()` and the same oversized length `bytesToRead` into the gzip filter as its output buffer and output budget.

Sink call. zlib now treats the output window as `maxlen = bytesToRead` bytes even though the heap buffer from step 6 is only 24,576 bytes long. The sanitizer reports the resulting one-byte write past that allocation in `inflate_fast`.

allocation_stack.function: QArrayData::allocate(unsigned long, unsigned long, unsigned long, QFlags<QArrayData::AllocationOption>)

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The fine-trace sink is the project `inflate(&d->zStream, Z_SYNC_FLUSH)` call that immediately invokes the crashing library frame `inflate_fast` reported by ASan.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan's allocation context points to the undersized dummy buffer at step 6 (line 249); the root cause is the immediately following step 7 that reuses that buffer with the larger `bytesToRead` length.

poc.trigger: Feed the staged 782-byte PoC to `karchive_fuzzer`; in the `KTar(gzipKD.get())` handler, `KTar::openArchive` reaches `KCompressionDevice::seek`, which overflows its dummy heap buffer while inflating the gzip stream.

format.name: GZip-compressed TAR stream
format.contract: A gzip-compressed tar input that makes `KCompressionDevice::seek` compute `bytesToRead > 3 * BUFFER_SIZE` for a `dev->seek(dev->pos() + skip)` call during `KTar::openArchive`, while enough compressed data remains for zlib to emit at least 24,577 output bytes into that call's dummy buffer.
